frente: Five days after an anterior myocardial infarction, a 64-year-old man suddenly becomes hypotensive with distended neck veins and pulseless electrical activity. What is the most likely complication?
verso: Left ventricular free wall rupture with cardiac tamponade
extra: Risk peaks around days 3 to 7 and persists for about 2 weeks: macrophages have removed the necrotic myocytes, but little collagen has been laid down, so the infarct is at its softest. Blood fills the pericardial sac and stops diastolic filling.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Contraction band necrosis in reperfused myocardium is caused by a massive influx of {{c1::calcium}} into injured myocytes.
extra: Restored flow delivers Ca<sup>2+</sup> to cells with damaged membranes; myofibrils hypercontract and form dense eosinophilic bands. Reperfusion also generates free radicals, so some salvageable tissue is lost.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: What is the most important risk factor for aortic dissection in adults older than 40 years?
extra: Chronic pressure overload narrows the vasa vasorum and causes ischemic degeneration of the aortic media, so an intimal tear can propagate along the weakened wall. In younger patients, connective tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome dominate.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Phase 2 (plateau) of the ventricular myocyte action potential is sustained by influx through {{c1::L-type Ca<sup>2+</sup>}} channels balanced by K<sup>+</sup> efflux.
extra: The Ca<sup>2+</sup> entering in the plateau triggers Ca<sup>2+</sup>-induced Ca<sup>2+</sup> release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, linking excitation to contraction. Non-dihydropyridine blockers such as verapamil reduce this current and contractility.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: In a healthy heart, which intrinsic mechanism raises stroke volume when venous return increases?
extra: Greater end-diastolic volume stretches sarcomeres toward optimal actin-myosin overlap and increases myofilament sensitivity to Ca<sup>2+</sup>, so the ventricle ejects more without any change in sympathetic tone.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: A 19-year-old athlete has a systolic murmur at the left sternal border that becomes louder during the strain phase of a Valsalva maneuver. Most likely diagnosis?
verso: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with LV outflow tract obstruction
extra: Straining lowers venous return and LV volume, which brings the hypertrophied septum and the anterior mitral leaflet closer and worsens outflow obstruction. Aortic stenosis murmurs soften with the same maneuver.
fonte: Braunwald's Heart Disease, 12th ed.

frente: Flecainide, a class IC antiarrhythmic, blocks {{c1::Na<sup>+</sup>}} channels and dissociates from them slowly, so it widens the QRS complex most at fast heart rates.
extra: Slow unbinding produces strong use dependence. In the CAST trial, class IC drugs increased mortality after myocardial infarction, so they are avoided in structural heart disease.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, sacubitril (given with valsartan) inhibits which enzyme?
extra: Neprilysin degrades natriuretic peptides, so its inhibition increases natriuresis and vasodilation; it also degrades angiotensin II, hence the pairing with an ARB. Because neprilysin breaks down bradykinin too, combining sacubitril with an ACE inhibitor raises the risk of angioedema, and a 36-hour washout is required.
nota_pt: No Brasil a associação é vendida como sacubitril-valsartana.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: Nitrates relieve exertional angina mainly through venodilation, which lowers {{c1::preload}} and therefore myocardial O<sub>2</sub> demand.
extra: Nitric oxide activates soluble guanylyl cyclase; cGMP leads to myosin light-chain dephosphorylation and smooth muscle relaxation, most strongly in veins at therapeutic doses.
nota_pt: Associar com inibidor da PDE-5 (sildenafila) pode causar hipotensão grave.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: An inferior STEMI is accompanied by complete heart block. Occlusion of which coronary artery is most likely?
extra: In most hearts the right coronary artery gives rise to the posterior descending artery (right dominance) and to the AV nodal artery, so inferior infarcts often cause bradycardia and AV block. In left-dominant hearts, both come from the circumflex.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: A 30-year-old man who injects drugs has fever and a new holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that increases with inspiration. Most likely organism?
extra: Surface adhesins let S. aureus colonize previously normal valves, and particulate matter in injected drugs is thought to damage right-sided valves. Tricuspid vegetations embolize to the lungs as septic pulmonary emboli.
fonte: Sherris Medical Microbiology, 7th ed.

frente: Molecular mimicry between cardiac myosin and which group A streptococcal antigen underlies acute rheumatic fever?
extra: Antibodies and T cells raised against M protein cross-react with cardiac and valvular antigens (a type II hypersensitivity reaction), producing pancarditis weeks after untreated pharyngitis.
nota_pt: No Brasil, a cardiopatia reumática continua sendo causa importante de valvopatia, sobretudo mitral.
fonte: Abbas Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 10th ed.

frente: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is most often caused by mutations in genes encoding {{c1::sarcomere}} proteins, with {{c2::autosomal dominant}} inheritance.
extra: Defective contractile proteins (most often beta-myosin heavy chain or myosin-binding protein C) lead to myocyte hypertrophy and disarray. It is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes, so first-degree relatives are screened.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 8th ed.

frente: A 12-year-old has tendon xanthomas and an LDL cholesterol of 600 mg/dL; both parents had premature coronary disease. Which protein is most likely defective?
extra: Without functional receptors, hepatocytes cannot clear LDL by endocytosis, and the lack of intracellular cholesterol keeps HMG-CoA reductase active. Homozygotes reach extreme LDL levels and develop atherosclerosis in childhood.
fonte: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 8th ed.

frente: Which junctions in the intercalated discs electrically couple adjacent cardiomyocytes?
extra: Connexin channels (mainly connexin-43 in ventricles) let ions pass between cells, so the myocardium depolarizes as a functional syncytium. Desmosomes and fasciae adherentes in the same discs provide mechanical attachment.
fonte: Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed.

frente: In a lung region distal to a pulmonary embolus, what value does the ventilation/perfusion ratio approach?
extra: The region is ventilated but not perfused, so its alveolar gas resembles inspired air. Blood is diverted to other regions, which become relatively overperfused (low V/Q) and cause hypoxemia.
fonte: West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

frente: A man is hypoxemic after an opioid overdose and his chest x-ray is clear. What A-a oxygen gradient is expected?
extra: Hypoventilation raises alveolar PCO<sub>2</sub> and lowers alveolar PO<sub>2</sub>; arterial PO<sub>2</sub> falls in parallel, so the gap does not widen. Supplemental O<sub>2</sub> or restored ventilation corrects it.
fonte: West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

frente: Which cell type proliferates to regenerate the alveolar epithelium after injury?
extra: Type II cells act as progenitors and differentiate into thin type I cells, which cover most of the alveolar surface but cannot divide. They also secrete surfactant.
fonte: Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed.

frente: The main surface-active lipid of pulmonary surfactant is {{c1::dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine}}.
extra: By the law of Laplace (P = 2T/r), small alveoli would collapse into large ones; surfactant lowers surface tension most where the radius is smallest. Maternal glucocorticoids accelerate its production in preterm fetuses.
nota_pt: A DPPC é uma lecitina; daí a relação lecitina/esfingomielina no líquido amniótico como índice de maturidade pulmonar fetal.
fonte: West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

frente: The most common CFTR mutation, F508del, causes cystic fibrosis mainly through which defect?
verso: Protein misfolding with retention and degradation in the ER
extra: The misfolded channel is recognized by ER quality control and degraded by the proteasome, so little CFTR reaches the apical membrane. CFTR correctors (such as elexacaftor and tezacaftor) target this folding defect.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 8th ed.

frente: By what mechanism does ivacaftor improve chloride transport in cystic fibrosis?
verso: It potentiates CFTR opening (increases open probability)
extra: Ivacaftor acts on channels already at the cell surface, so it works best in gating mutations such as G551D. For F508del it is combined with correctors that bring more protein to the membrane.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: A 68-year-old smoker who recently stayed at a hotel with a cooling tower has high fever, diarrhea, confusion, lobar pneumonia and a serum sodium of 128 mEq/L. Most likely organism?
extra: The bacterium lives in aerosolized water and replicates inside alveolar macrophages, so it is not spread person to person. It stains poorly on Gram stain; diagnosis uses the urinary antigen test (serogroup 1) or culture on buffered charcoal yeast extract.
fonte: Sherris Medical Microbiology, 7th ed.

frente: Mycobacterium tuberculosis survives inside macrophages mainly by blocking {{c1::phagosome-lysosome fusion}}.
extra: Cell wall glycolipids (mannose-capped lipoarabinomannan; review books also cite sulfatides) arrest phagosome maturation, so the bacilli escape acidification and lysosomal enzymes and keep multiplying until a Th1 response activates the macrophage.
fonte: Sherris Medical Microbiology, 7th ed.

frente: Which Th1 cytokine activates infected macrophages and drives granuloma formation in tuberculosis?
extra: Macrophages present mycobacterial antigens and secrete IL-12, which polarizes CD4<sup>+</sup> cells to Th1. TNF-α maintains the granuloma, so anti-TNF therapy can reactivate latent infection.
nota_pt: Antes de iniciar anti-TNF, rastrear tuberculose latente (prova tuberculínica ou IGRA).
fonte: Abbas Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 10th ed.

frente: A retired shipyard worker had pleural plaques for years and now has a pleural mass encasing the lung with a hemorrhagic effusion. Most likely diagnosis?
extra: Long, thin asbestos fibers reach the pleura and cause chronic injury and oxidative DNA damage over decades. Bronchogenic carcinoma is still the more common cancer in exposed workers and, unlike mesothelioma, is strongly potentiated by smoking.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Small cell lung carcinoma can cause euvolemic hyponatremia through ectopic secretion of {{c1::ADH (vasopressin)}}.
extra: The tumor arises from neuroendocrine cells, which explains its paraneoplastic hormone production. Inappropriate ADH increases free water reabsorption in collecting ducts, producing concentrated urine despite low plasma osmolality.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Montelukast prevents bronchoconstriction in asthma by blocking which receptor?
extra: Leukotrienes C<sub>4</sub>, D<sub>4</sub> and E<sub>4</sub>, made via 5-lipoxygenase, cause bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion and edema. Blocking their receptor is especially useful in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, where arachidonic acid is shunted toward leukotrienes.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: In a patient who aspirates while upright, which lobe is most often involved?
extra: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left, so particles follow it into the basal segments. In the supine position, the posterior segment of the upper lobe and the superior segment of the lower lobe are favored.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: How does angiotensin II constriction of the efferent arteriole change the filtration fraction?
extra: Glomerular capillary pressure rises, so GFR is preserved while renal plasma flow falls. This is why ACE inhibitors can sharply reduce GFR in bilateral renal artery stenosis, where filtration depends on efferent tone.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: Thiazide diuretics block the {{c1::Na<sup>+</sup>/Cl<sup>−</sup> cotransporter}} in the distal convoluted tubule, which increases Ca<sup>2+</sup> reabsorption.
extra: Lower intracellular Na<sup>+</sup> enhances basolateral Na<sup>+</sup>/Ca<sup>2+</sup> exchange and apical Ca<sup>2+</sup> entry. This makes thiazides useful in hypercalciuria with calcium stones and explains mild hypercalcemia as an adverse effect.
nota_pt: Hidroclorotiazida e clortalidona são as mais usadas no Brasil.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: A 25-year-old man has hemoptysis and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis; immunofluorescence shows linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane. Which antigen is targeted?
verso: Alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen (NC1 domain)
extra: The same collagen chain is present in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes, so autoantibodies cause crescentic glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage (type II hypersensitivity). Antibody bound evenly along the membrane produces the linear pattern, unlike the granular deposits of immune complexes.
nota_pt: Doença antimembrana basal glomerular (síndrome de Goodpasture).
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Two weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis, a 7-year-old has periorbital edema, cola-colored urine and hypertension. What does immunofluorescence of a renal biopsy show?
extra: Immune complexes deposit as subepithelial humps and activate complement, which lowers serum C3 and recruits neutrophils. The pattern is granular because the complexes are discrete, unlike the linear pattern of anti-GBM disease.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Most cases of primary membranous nephropathy are caused by autoantibodies against the podocyte antigen {{c1::PLA<sub>2</sub>R (phospholipase A<sub>2</sub> receptor)}}.
extra: Antibodies bind the antigen in situ, forming subepithelial deposits that activate complement and injure podocytes, producing nephrotic-range proteinuria. Secondary forms are linked to hepatitis B, lupus, solid tumors and drugs.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 4-year-old has nephrotic syndrome and a normal-appearing biopsy on light microscopy. What does electron microscopy show?
extra: Podocyte injury disrupts the slit diaphragm and the charge barrier, producing selective albuminuria. It is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and usually responds to corticosteroids.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Mutation of which gene causes most cases of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease?
extra: Polycystin-1 regulates tubular cell proliferation through the primary cilium; a second somatic hit in a tubule cell starts cyst growth. PKD1 disease is more severe than PKD2 disease and progresses to kidney failure earlier.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 8th ed.

frente: In a primary metabolic acidosis, Winter's formula predicts the expected PaCO<sub>2</sub> as {{c1::1.5×[HCO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>] + 8 ± 2}}.
extra: Peripheral chemoreceptors sense the acidemia and increase ventilation. A measured PaCO<sub>2</sub> above the predicted range indicates a coexisting respiratory acidosis; below it, a coexisting respiratory alkalosis.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is associated with loss of the {{c1::VHL}} tumor suppressor gene on chromosome {{c2::3p}}.
extra: Without VHL protein, hypoxia-inducible factor is not degraded and drives VEGF and erythropoietin expression. This explains the vascular tumors, possible polycythemia and the use of VEGF pathway inhibitors in treatment.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 52-year-old man with long-standing heartburn has a biopsy of the distal esophagus showing columnar epithelium with goblet cells. Diagnosis?
extra: Chronic acid reflux drives metaplasia of the stratified squamous epithelium into intestinal-type columnar epithelium, which tolerates acid better. Dysplasia in this tissue is the main precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: A 40-year-old has progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids and a bird's beak on barium swallow. Loss of which neurons explains the disease?
extra: Without inhibitory input, the lower esophageal sphincter fails to relax and esophageal peristalsis is lost. Chronic Chagas disease (Trypanosoma cruzi) destroys the same plexus and produces an identical picture.
nota_pt: No Brasil, lembrar do megaesôfago chagásico nas áreas endêmicas.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Which enzyme lets Helicobacter pylori survive in the acidic gastric lumen?
extra: Urease converts urea to ammonia and CO<sub>2</sub>; ammonia buffers acid around the bacterium. The same reaction is the basis of the urea breath test and the rapid urease test on biopsy.
fonte: Sherris Medical Microbiology, 7th ed.

frente: Proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole irreversibly inhibit the parietal cell {{c1::H<sup>+</sup>/K<sup>+</sup>-ATPase}}.
extra: They are prodrugs activated in the acidic secretory canaliculus, where they bind the pump covalently. Acid secretion returns only as new pumps are synthesized, so a once-daily dose works despite a short plasma half-life.
fonte: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, 15th ed.

frente: {{c1::Cholecystokinin}}, released by duodenal I cells in response to fatty acids and amino acids, contracts the gallbladder and relaxes the sphincter of Oddi.
extra: It also stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion and slows gastric emptying, matching delivery of chyme to digestive capacity. Its effect on the pancreas is partly mediated by vagal reflexes.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: Secretin, released by duodenal S cells when acid enters the duodenum, stimulates pancreatic {{c1::bicarbonate}} secretion.
extra: Bicarbonate neutralizes gastric acid and brings the duodenal pH into the range where pancreatic enzymes work. Secretin also inhibits gastric acid secretion, closing the feedback loop.
fonte: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

frente: A healthy 22-year-old develops mild jaundice during a fast; unconjugated bilirubin is elevated and liver enzymes are normal. Reduced activity of which enzyme explains this?
extra: A promoter variant lowers expression of the enzyme that conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid. Fasting, illness and exertion increase the bilirubin load and unmask the mild deficit; there is no hemolysis or liver injury.
fonte: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 8th ed.

frente: In acetaminophen overdose, necrosis is most severe in which zone of the hepatic acinus?
extra: Zone 3 hepatocytes have the highest CYP2E1 activity, which converts excess acetaminophen to the reactive metabolite NAPQI. Once glutathione is depleted, NAPQI binds cell proteins and kills the cells.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Acetaminophen overdose is treated with {{c1::N-acetylcysteine}}, which replenishes hepatic glutathione.
extra: It supplies cysteine for glutathione synthesis, so NAPQI is conjugated before it binds hepatocyte proteins. It works best when started within 8 hours of ingestion.
nota_pt: No Brasil, acetilcisteína por via intravenosa ou oral.
fonte: Goodman & Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 14th ed.

frente: A peptic ulcer on the posterior wall of the duodenal bulb erodes into which artery, causing massive bleeding?
extra: The gastroduodenal artery, a branch of the common hepatic artery, runs directly behind the first part of the duodenum. Anterior duodenal ulcers tend to perforate into the peritoneal cavity instead.
fonte: Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th ed.

frente: A 48-year-old woman has pruritus, fatigue and a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase. Which serum autoantibody most strongly suggests primary biliary cholangitis?
extra: The antibody targets the E2 subunit of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. T cells destroy small intrahepatic bile ducts, causing cholestasis that can progress to cirrhosis.
fonte: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

frente: Familial adenomatous polyposis results from a germline mutation in the {{c1::APC}} gene on chromosome {{c2::5q}}.
extra: APC normally targets β-catenin for degradation; when the second allele is lost, β-catenin accumulates and activates Wnt target genes. Hundreds of adenomas develop, and colorectal cancer is almost certain without colectomy.
fonte: Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 8th ed.

frente: Which cells at the base of small intestinal crypts secrete defensins and lysozyme?
extra: Their eosinophilic apical granules release antimicrobial peptides that shape the microbiota and protect the neighboring stem cells. Paneth cell dysfunction is linked to Crohn disease of the ileum.
fonte: Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed.
